transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-09
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Morales - Redwood (AE), Marcus Chen - Redwood (SE), Ava Patel - Redwood (CSM); Priya Desai - Argent (CISO), Roberto Martinez - Argent (Head of Platform), Mei Lin - Argent (Security Engineer), Samir Rao - Argent (DevOps)

Summary (auto): Quick posture review of Redwood SOC 2 and ISO artifacts, discuss controls mapping, trust center access, encryption/KMS, RBAC/SSO integration, data residency and audit logs. Agree to share artifacts and a controls mapping spreadsheet; follow-up next week.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena (Redwood AE): Hi everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick intro, I'm Lena, AE on the account, Marcus is our SE, Ava from CS. How's everyone doing over at Argent?
[00:08] Priya (Argent CISO): Good thanks, Priya here. We're short on time but wanted to run through your SOC 2 / ISO posture and make sure we understand how Redwood maps to our control set.
[00:16] Lena: Absolutely. The goal is to show you the reports we have, give Trust Center access, and walk controls mapping. Marcus will cover the technical controls.
[00:24] Marcus (Redwood SE): Hey all — I'll focus on the infra/security bits: RBAC, SSO/SAML, KMS integration, audit logs, data residency. I'll try not to steamroll, promise.
[00:33] Roberto (Argent): Quick ask up front — we have an external SOC 2 audit planned in Q2 and need to know if Redwood's evidence and trust artifacts are sufficient for our auditors.
[00:41] Marcus: Understood. We have a SOC 2 Type II report, and ISO 27001 certificate. We can share the PDFs and also give read-only Trust Center access where we host mapping docs and control narratives.
[00:50] Mei (Argent SE): When you say Trust Center, is that a link? Can you show where the control mapping lives?
[00:57] Lena: Yes, we can add you to trust.redwood.com or send a one-time link. We'll include a controls mapping spreadsheet — it's pre-populated for common control frameworks and we annotate which controls are covered by Redwood, which require customer implementation, and which are joint.
[01:10] Priya: Great. A few specific things: full disk encryption at rest, KMS/bring-your-own-key, audit log retention and tamper evidence, SSO + SCIM for provisioning, and data residency for EU and US.
[01:22] Marcus: Good list. Quick notes: disks are encrypted at rest — we use AES-256 at the hypervisor and storage layer; for hosted customers we support KMS integrations and BYOK for Dedicated/Private deployments. On hosted we use provider-managed keys by default unless you opt for a dedicated KMS setup.
[01:37] Samir (Argent DevOps): Is BYOK available for your hosted multi-tenant offering or only Dedicated/Private?
[01:41] Marcus: BYOK is available for Dedicated capacity and Private deployments; for hosted, we offer customer-managed keys via our dedicated tenancy option or via a partner plugin — there are a few caveats and we'll capture in the controls mapping.
[01:51] Speaker 1: (mumbled) KV cash, kv cache — sorry, "KV cache" — related to how session data is persisted and whether that shows up in logs.
[01:57] Marcus: Yeah, KV cache is ephemeral in the serving runtime; we don't persist per-customer KV caches to long-term storage by default. That reduces risk but we can document behavior per deployment type.
[02:06] Priya: How about audit logs — what granularity, and do you provide integrity checks or append-only storage?
[02:12] Marcus: We emit structured audit logs for admin actions, model deploys, key rotations, and API access events. Logs are written to an append-only store with checksums; for Dedicated we can push to customer S3/Cloud Storage or stream to customer SIEM via forwarders. Retention defaults to 90 days for hosted but is configurable for enterprise customers.
[02:29] Roberto: For our auditors, we need at least 12 months retention. Can you extend?
[02:33] Marcus: Yes — for enterprise/Dedicated we support retention policies to 12+ months, and we can provide exports for audits. We'll note that in the mapping.
[02:41] Mei: SSO — we use Okta and need SCIM provisioning and role mappings that align with our RBAC. How granular is Redwood's RBAC?
[02:49] Marcus: Our RBAC supports org roles, project roles, and token-level scopes. You can map IdP groups to Redwood roles via SAML assertions or SCIM provisioning. For higher assurance we recommend provisioning + Just-In-Time groups and limit admin scopes to a small set.
[03:02] Priya: Do we get audit trail that ties SSO logins to actions?
[03:06] Marcus: Yes, auth events include the SAML subject. We store auth logs with user principal and tie them to API tokens and actions in the audit stream.
[03:13] Lena: Quick interjection — common auditor question: do you have any non-repudiation or tamper evidence? Marcus touched on append-only with checksums, but we can also provide a chain-of-custody note for logs. We'll add a short write-up.
[03:25] Priya: That'd be helpful. Also curious about vulnerability management and patch cadence for your runtime.
[03:31] Marcus: We run regular vulnerability scans, monthly patch cycles, and emergency patches for critical CVEs. We publish an incident response playbook in the Trust Center and provide CVE notices to customers for Dedicated instances.
[03:42] Samir: Data residency — our primary concern is EU data staying in EU region. Does Redwood guarantee region pinning for hosted?
[03:49] Marcus: We support region pinning for data and compute in hosted for certain regions; for stricter guarantees we recommend Dedicated or Private. We'll include a matrix in the mapping showing guarantees and where they apply.
[04:00] Roberto: Encryption in transit — TLS versions, cipher suites?
[04:03] Marcus: TLS 1.2+ and we prefer 1.3 where supported, modern cipher suites only. We can share our crypto spec in the Trust Center.
[04:10] Mei: A couple of micro questions — do you retain prompts or inputs for model telemetry? How long and can we opt out?
[04:18] Marcus: By default we retain telemetry for service quality — request metadata and anonymized prompt traces — for 90 days. For enterprise we offer options to disable prompt retention and to enable strict non-retention for PII-sensitive flows; we can also provide on-prem package.
[04:31] Priya: Is there end-to-end encryption for user payloads with BYOK? Meaning even Redwood can't read data?
[04:37] Marcus: With a true BYOK + customer-managed KMS in Private deployment, keys never leave customer control and logs/objects can be encrypted with those keys. For hosted standard model we have to decrypt to run inference so the platform processes the plaintext. We can discuss proxying or running inference in customer-controlled enclaves for extra assurance.
[04:53] Lena: I'm going to share the Trust Center link in the chat and upload the SOC 2 and ISO cert now, and Marcus will follow up with the mapping spreadsheet.
[04:59] [screen share note] Lena shares trust.redwood.com/trust (link pasted) and an action sheet titled "controls-mapping-argent-template.xlsx"
[05:07] Priya: Looks good. One last question on penetration testing and third-party attestations. Who performs pentests and do you share results?
[05:13] Marcus: We work with third-party firms for annual penetration tests and Red team engagements; high-level summaries and remediation status are available in Trust Center. Raw reports are redacted but available under NDA for enterprise customers.
[05:24] Priya: Perfect. That helps us scope the auditor conversation.
[05:28] Roberto: For contractual obligations, we may need an updated DPA and security appendix. Who owns that?
[05:33] Lena: I'll loop in legal — we have a standard security appendix and DPA, and we can provide a mark-up to fit Argent's needs.
[05:38] Ava (CSM): I'll open a ticket and attach the DPA template after the call.
[05:41] Priya: Great. Next steps?
[05:43] Lena: Action items: we'll send SOC 2 Type II, ISO cert, Trust Center access, and controls mapping. You (Priya) will confirm the specific control set and auditors contacts. We'll reconvene next week to review the mapping.
[05:54] Priya: Sounds good — thanks everyone.
[05:57] Marcus: Thanks, we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and detailed notes on KMS and audit log exports.
[06:03] Lena: Thanks all — meeting adjourned.
